label: serial byte copies for tiny CPU lookups
hypothesis: Avoid torch CPU dispatch/thread-pool overhead for bulk gathers of <=8 tokens using serial byte copies into the existing pinned buffer. Baseline model profiles show 24/44 us CPU gather at b1/b8 decode; CPU microdiagnostic shows 4.68->2.70 us and 24.56->17.21 us for hot lookups. Confirm end-to-end effects independently.
expected_bottleneck: tiny bulk CPU table gather and associated CPU scheduling overhead
change: Precreate zero-copy uint8 NumPy views; copy each requested row for <=8 tokens when CPU table is contiguous. Fall back to torch index_select for other inputs. No value/lookup caching, dtype conversion, global thread changes or extra table storage.

screen.reason_no_batch16: Only CPU lookup implementation for <=8 tokens changes; transfer volume and pipeline scheduling remain fixed.

not_run.frozen_baseline_confirmation: Parent-relative confirmation failed retention criterion; inherited A0001 gain is not an A0002 gain
not_run.full_model_correctness: No retention nomination; small/model correctness gates already passed

limitations: Microdiagnostic uses hot rows and does not establish model gain; generation CPU scheduling causality remains unproven.
decision: Three independent parent-relative pairs did not establish both offload latency and absolute-gap reduction in any primary workload. Preserve modest positive decode estimates without acceptance; no measurement extension.
